idiom_name: rayon::join (work-stealing) + par_iter / par_sort for data-parallel leaves
implementation_notes: rayon supplies the fork/join: join(a, b) runs two closures potentially in parallel on a work-stealing pool and returns their pair, and the same pool backs par_iter and par_sort, so the classic task pool disappears. The borrow checker enforces the pattern's precondition - independent subproblems - because both closures would otherwise need a mutable borrow of the same slice; split_at_mut (or chunks_mut) is the idiom that makes the halves provably disjoint, and a closure that captures a non-Send handle simply does not compile. std::thread::scope is the manual fallback when rayon is not an acceptable dependency; joins are automatic at scope exit.
pitfalls: The closures passed to rayon::join must be Send: a captured Rc or raw-pointer wrapper fails to compile - the static encoding of the independence precondition.
Nesting join below the useful threshold makes rayon's per-task overhead visible; keep the cut-off or set with_min_len on parallel iterators.
Aliasing the same data in both closures is rejected by the borrow checker, and working around it with unsafe reintroduces exactly the races the pattern's precondition excludes.
